Six days after the assassination, the FBI recorded a lead about photographs. A memorandum dated November 28, 1963 states that Eddie Barker of KRLD reported that a man named Capp Field possessed photographs of the assassination. In those first days, every camera in Dealey Plaza mattered to investigators.

Amateur film and photographs became core evidence in the Kennedy case, because they fixed the shooting in frames. A report that one more man held pictures sent agents to find him. The memo preserves that lead as the Bureau logged it, part of the great gathering of images from Dallas.
